summary: Frontend-only verification of the new DUR (stop TTS) button feature. All 6 acceptance scenarios PASS (21/21 assertions). (T1) After sending 'Bana 3 cümlelik bir şiir oku': DUR button [data-testid=stop-speaking-button] appeared as an absolute red pulsing overlay inside the input bar; hud-top-left status showed 'DURUM: KONUŞUYOR'; clicking DUR hid the button, cleared audio.src, kept audio.paused=true, and status flipped to 'DURUM: BEKLEMEDE'. (T2) Early-phase stop during synthesis: DUR button appeared while ttsApi.synthesize was still in-flight (audio.src was still empty when we clicked); clicking DUR early invalidated speechIdRef; 8 seconds later audio.paused stayed true, audio.src stayed empty, and DUR button remained hidden — confirming the in-flight cancellation via speechIdRef token works. (T3) Escape key: page.keyboard.press('Escape') while speaking correctly stopped TTS (DUR hidden, audio paused, src cleared). (T4) Sphere click: clicking the central holographic canvas while speaking also stopped TTS (same effects). (T5) Voice OFF regression: after toggling [data-testid=voice-toggle] to off, sending 'Selam nasilsin' did NOT trigger speaking state and DUR button did not appear within 7.5 seconds; status remained BEKLEMEDE. (T6) Normal chat regression: typing 'Test mesajı' and pressing Enter cleared the input (message was sent). Screenshot captured shows the DUR button correctly overlaying the mic/input/send bar with 'DUR (ESC)' label and red pulse-glow.
critical_code_review_comments: SertexMain.jsx stopSpeaking() correctly increments speechIdRef.current BEFORE resetting audio — this ordering is important so that any in-flight speak() that resolves after stopSpeaking() checks (myId !== speechIdRef.current) and skips play(). Verified end-to-end in T2 (early-phase cancel).

SertexMain.jsx speak() properly guards against stale synthesis: 'if (myId !== speechIdRef.current) { revoke blob; return; }' — this prevents a canceled synthesis from setting audio.src or calling .play() after user hit DUR.
SertexMain.jsx keydown listener depends on [state] — closure captures current state so Escape only stops when state === 'speaking'. Good.

InputBar.jsx DUR button uses absolute inset-0 z-10 overlay covering the input row — visually blocks mic/input/send while speaking. Correct UX because those controls are irrelevant during TTS playback anyway. Screenshot confirms clean rendering with animate-pulse-glow.

HolographicSphere onClick handler in SertexMain: state==='speaking' branch stops TTS. However the outer wrapper div has pointer-events-none on the flex container but pointer-events-auto on the inner sphere div — click reached the canvas correctly in T4. No issue.

Minor: SertexMain.jsx state-effect useEffect (lines 111-117) uses `else if (state === 'speaking') return;` — this keeps state='speaking' locked until stopSpeaking() explicitly sets idle or audio onEnded fires. Correct. But the deps array is missing `state` (only [listening, thinking]) which the ESLint disable comment on line 176 hints is intentional; nonetheless the closure sees a stale `state` on each render — currently fine because the check reads state at effect-body time (not stale after re-render because effect re-runs on listening/thinking changes and state is a state var). Acceptable.

Minor: The keydown Escape listener does not preventDefault — Escape may still bubble to other listeners (e.g., a modal). Not a functional issue for this feature but worth noting if future modals add Escape-to-close behavior that could conflict.

context_for_next_testing_agent: DUR (stop TTS) feature is verified working end-to-end via 4 stop mechanisms: (1) DUR button click, (2) Escape key, (3) sphere click, (4) implicit — voice OFF prevents speaking altogether. Key testids: stop-speaking-button, tts-audio, chat-input, send-button, voice-toggle, hud-top-left. Note: in headless chromium the audio element may show paused=true throughout because autoplay is blocked, but the state='speaking' transition still happens (verified via hud-top-left text 'DURUM: KONUŞUYOR'). This means the DUR-button visibility (which is gated on speaking prop = state === 'speaking') is the primary functional check, not audio.play() success. speechIdRef token invalidation is the guard that prevents late-arriving synthesis from starting audio after stop — verified in T2 with 8-second post-stop poll. Overdue Task modal is dismissed via [data-testid=overdue-alert-close] after login.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature-addition verification. Mechanism: stopSpeaking() bumps speechIdRef.current++ (invalidates any in-flight speak()), then pauses audio, resets currentTime, removes src attribute, calls audio.load(), and revokes blob URL. It then setState('idle'). speak() captures myId=++speechIdRef.current at entry and checks !== speechIdRef.current after ttsApi.synthesize resolves — if bumped, revokes the blob URL without setting audio.src or calling play(). This closes the race window between clicking DUR and TTS synthesis finishing on the server. DUR button visibility is bound to prop speaking=(state==='speaking') passed to InputBar, rendering an absolute inset-0 overlay covering the input row. Escape key handler registered on window filters e.key==='Escape' && state==='speaking'. Sphere onClick early-returns to stopSpeaking() when state==='speaking'.
